[34mInvestigated:[0m Traced Scheduler.run_pending, run_all, _run_job, and Job.run in schedule/__init__.py, plus the existing exception-handling docs and the test layout in test_schedule.py. Confirmed that an exception in Job.run skipped last_run and _schedule_next_run, which left the failed job due.

[33mLearned:[0m Before the change, an exception in one due job stopped the sorted loop in run_pending, so later due jobs did not run in that tick. Because the failed job was never rescheduled, it stayed due and re-ran on every run_pending call, which could starve jobs sorted after it. run_all has no exception handling and still stops at the first failure.

[32mCompleted:[0m run_pending now wraps each job in try/except Exception, runs every due job, re-raises the first exception after the loop, and logs later ones with logger.exception. Job.run now updates last_run and calls _schedule_next_run in a finally block, so failed jobs are rescheduled. run_all sleeps only between jobs. Four new tests were added covering remaining jobs running after a failure, failed-job rescheduling, extra failures being logged, and the run_all sleep count. The failure-ordering test was changed to force past next_run values instead of relying on wall-clock sleeps. The full suite passes at 85 tests, up from 81. docs/exception-handling.rst was updated to describe the new behavior. Nothing has been committed.

[35mNext Steps:[0m The run_pending and Job.run changes are in place and tested. Possible next work: decide whether run_all should get the same per-job isolation, and check whether _schedule_next_run raising inside the finally block should be guarded so it does not mask the job's original exception.

[36mNotes:[0m Behavior change: a job that raises is now rescheduled where it previously stayed due and retried on the next tick. Anyone depending on retry-on-failure would notice. Only the first exception is re-raised, not bundled. Bundling would need ExceptionGroup, which is unavailable on older supported Pythons. A failed job that is past its until() deadline is cancelled on the next tick, not immediately, because the overdue check after execution is skipped when job_func raises.
